title: EIDD-3525 is a broad-spectrum antiviral against alphavirus infection that targets the nsP4 RNA-dependent RNA polymerase.
journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
abstract: Mosquito-transmitted alphaviruses, including chikungunya (CHIKV), Mayaro, Eastern equine encephalitis, and Venezuelan equine encephalitis viruses, cause severe arthritic or neurologic disease in humans. There are currently no approved antiviral treatments against alphavirus infection. Here, we report that the purine ribonucleoside EIDD-3525 is a potent inhibitor of alphavirus replication in vitro with broad spectrum antiviral activity against the Alphavirus genus. Using a trans-replicase assay, we find that EIDD-3525 blocks alphavirus RNA replication. Mutational profiling suggests that EIDD-3525 targets the alphavirus nsP4 RNA-dependent RNA polymerase that is conserved across medically important alphaviruses. In a pre-clinical mouse model of CHIKV infection and disease, oral treatment with EIDD-3525 reduced viral tissue burdens and the severity of virus-induced disease. Collectively, our findings support the continued development of the purine ribonucleoside EIDD-3525 as an orally available antiviral therapeutic for use against a broad group of alphaviruses.

title: Biomarker Approach for Differentiating Boldenone Administration From Ex Vivo Formation in Colt Urine.
abstract: Boldenone is a prohibited anabolic-androgenic steroid in equine sports, but also endogenous in colts with an International Threshold of 15 ng/mL in urine. Recently, its presence was demonstrated at very low concentrations in the urine of other genders, resulting in the establishment of biomarker approaches, based on the detection of Δ1-progesterone and 20α-dihydro-Δ1-progesterone, to distinguish drug administrations from microbial sources (altered feeds and ex vivo formation in urine). In the current study, the applicability of these biomarkers in colt urine was assessed by quantitative analysis of 121 samples. Boldenone was detected in all samples (24-8420 pg/mL), Δ1-progesterone was only detected in one sample ( 50 pg/mL or 20α-dihydro-Δ1-progesterone > 100 pg/mL indicates a microbial origin) could be applied to colt urine samples with boldenone concentrations exceeding the International Threshold. This approach can be used to give confidence that reported findings in colts are caused by steroid administrations rather than microbial activity.

title: Renal dysplasia in horses: 25 cases (1991-2021).
abstract: Renal dysplasia (RD) is a congenital malformation with variable clinical expression and limited characterization in horses. We hypothesized that RD occurs in horses across a broad age range and may be overrepresented in specific breeds. Our objective was to describe clinical, clinicopathologic, and histopathologic findings in horses with RD. Twenty-five horses with RD identified from a veterinary teaching hospital between 1991 and 2021. Horses included neonates, young horses, and adults, with ages ranging from 0 days to 24 years and representing multiple breeds and both sexes. Retrospective case series including review of laboratory data, ultrasonographic findings, treatment, outcome, and histopathology. Breed prevalence was assessed using Fisher's exact test. Outcomes included age and breed distribution, clinical and laboratory abnormalities, and diagnostic findings associated with RD. Renal dysplasia was bilateral in 84% of cases and diffuse in 68%. Eleven horses (44%) had RD as an incidental necropsy finding. Clinical signs were more common in neonates, with azotemia in 64% and hyponatremia in 37%. Neurologic signs were reported in 58% of neonates. Paint horses (odds ratio [OR]: 21.3; 95% CI, 8.0-56.7) and Miniature horses (OR: 12.9; 95% CI, 4.4-37.7) were overrepresented compared with all other breeds combined (P < .0001). Histopathologic findings included primitive mesenchyme (32%), retention of fetal glomeruli (24%), and tubular dysplasia (24%). RD was confirmed by biopsy in one horse; in 2 others, biopsy findings were suggestive but not definitive, requiring necropsy confirmation. Renal dysplasia affects a variety of breeds and ages of horses, including both sexes. Paint horses and Miniature horses were overrepresented. Renal dysplasia ranges from subclinical to causing severe kidney disease. Affected neonatal foals are more likely to have clinical signs.

title: One Health genomic surveillance of ticks found on community-dwelling non-human 'farm' animals to identify microbes associated with tick borne illnesses in Eastern Ontario.
abstract: Companion animals, such as dogs and cats, and wildlife are recognized as sentinel species in One Health surveillance due to periodic exposure to ticks and infection by tick-borne pathogens (TBPs). Surveillance of this type is a strategy that captures a broad range of genetic, immunological, and behavioral factors that affect tick and disease dynamics. In contrast, non-human animals (hereafter referred to as 'animals') that are traditionally farmed for their meat and other products have been largely overlooked as sentinel species. Community-dwelling farm sanctuary residents, such as cattle, pigs, horses, and other traditionally 'farmed' animals have close daily contact with human caregivers, making them excellent candidates for One Health surveillance. These animals, often free-range in pastures and/or woodlands, bridging the territory inhabited by wildlife and that occupied by humans. This study collected 67 ticks, from bovines (n = 22), equines (n = 35) and canines (n = 6) residing in a farm animal sanctuary and screened them for microbes associated with tick borne illnesses using 16S rRNA V4 amplicon targeted sequencing (515F/906R) with custom Rickettsia buchneri blocking primers to boost sensitivity. Only 60 ticks were viable for analysis, 59 were of Ixodes species and one was Dermacentor variabilis. Of these, 31.6% (n = 19) tested positive for potential pathogens, including 21.6% (n = 13) for the causative agent of Lyme disease (Borrelia burgdorferi) and 15% (n = 9) for Anaplasma phagocytophilum, with a co-infection rate of five percent (n = 3). Utilizing community dwelling sanctuary residents allowed us to detect potential threats to both animal and human health and was instrumental in the rapid diagnosis of anaplasmosis in two study participants (a horse and a pony) who showed symptoms of lethargy and inappetence after being bitten by ticks.

title: The dependence of Rev-mediated nuclear export of EIAV mRNA on Rev multimerization is modulated by mRNA length.
abstract: All lentiviruses encode a regulatory protein, Rev, which mediates nuclear export of viral mRNAs and is required for viral replication, and multimerization of Rev is thought to be critical for its function. The lentivirus equine infectious anemia virus (EIAV) Rev is known to mediate the nuclear export of long-length, unspliced, or incompletely spliced viral mRNA encoding the viral structural proteins (Gag, Pol, and Env), like Rev from other lentiviruses. However, EIAV Rev also mediates the nuclear export of a short-length, fully spliced viral mRNA species encoding the functionally unknown protein Mat. Here, we found that disruption of Rev multimerization impaired Rev activity in mediating nuclear export and expression of gag-pol mRNA, but not in mediating nuclear export and expression of mat mRNA. Deficiency of Rev multimerization leads to lower viral replication. Further investigation revealed that the activity of multimerization-deficient Revs in mediating nuclear export and expression of long-length EIAV or HIV-1 mRNAs was significantly lower than that of wild-type Rev, while this difference was significantly reduced or absent between the two in mediating nuclear export and expression of short-length EIAV or HIV-1 mRNAs. This suggests that the differential dependence of the nuclear export of gag-pol mRNA and mat mRNA on Rev multimerization is modulated by the lengths of the mRNA species. Our findings suggest that when targeting short mRNAs, EIAV Rev appears to be able to perform nuclear export activity in a non-multimerized state.IMPORTANCEMultimerization of lentiviral Rev is thought to be essential for its function, which is to mediate nuclear export of viral mRNA, a necessary step in lentiviral replication. In equine infectious anemia virus (EIAV), the nuclear export of unspliced viral mRNAs encoding structural proteins (Gag/Pol) is dependent on Rev. Moreover, our recent studies have demonstrated that the nuclear export of a fully spliced mRNA species, mat, encoding a small protein (Mat) of unknown function, is also Rev-dependent. In this study, we observed that the expression and nuclear export of EIAV gag-pol mRNA were strictly dependent on Rev multimerization, whereas those of mat mRNA were not. Interestingly, we also determined that the dependence of Rev-mediated nuclear export of EIAV mRNA on Rev multimerization is strongly associated with lengths of these mRNA species. Our data imply that EIAV Rev is able to exert nuclear export activity in a non-multimerized state.

title: From the bit to the between: an autoethnography of friendship.
abstract: To develop any depth of understanding of friendships, there is a need to integrate holistic epistemological practices that respect the fluid relational and emergent nature of the between space where friends meet. This recognizes friendship as an experience always in process, never a thing or anything like a thing. Multispecies autoethnography is especially well suited to exploring such meetings, for it is concerned with issues of justice, power and freedom and therefore with addressing anthropocentricity. In this study, this qualitative methodology is presented and then developed to provide the reader with a rich ethnographic sense of the author's concerns about the quality of relationship made possible by the traditional bit and the need to prototype and demonstrate co-created alternatives. The work of Simone Weil on attention and Martin Buber on dialogue is emphasized throughout, as a theoretical framework for understanding the ways relationships founded on attentive listening and attunement can be nurtured in partnership. This example is full of misunderstandings and mismeetings, necessitating forgiveness on a regular basis and a commitment to show up, be present and relate. This study is not about friendships between conspecifics; it is about relationality and relational practice and how we practice working equine welfare, through the nurturing of humility and power literacy. This study offers insights and vocabulary that can help the reader develop an awareness-based systems change approach to equine welfare; one that involves listening to ourselves, learning to see, sense, and presence; one that, ultimately, allows equids and humans to nurture the between space where friendship can take root and grow. In doing so, this study provides insights into the possibilities of One Health justice.

title: A Trojan horse nanoplatform overcoming delivery barriers for targeted gene immunotherapy of colorectal cancer.
abstract: Programmed cell death ligand 1 (PD-L1) antibody has been shown to hold tremendous promise in curing metastatic colorectal cancer (CRC). However, the delivery efficacy of the targeted biologics limits this immunotherapy in a subset of CRC. Here we report a novel biomimetic 'Trojan horse' nano-delivery system for targeted gene-immunotherapy of colorectal cancer. The system comprises a core of gold nanoparticles and cationic liposomes encapsulating CRISPR/Cas9-sgSOX9, camouflaged with homologous CRC cell membranes for immune evasion and tumor tropism, and functionalized with PD-L1 antibodies to enhance tumor recognition and relieve immune suppression. In vitro, the nano-system potently suppressed CRC cell proliferation, migration and invasion. in vivo, it exhibited robust tumor-targeting specificity, favorable preliminary biosafety profile and marked inhibition of tumor growth in subcutaneous xenograft models. Mechanistically, the system remodeled the tumor microenvironment by promoting CD8+ T-cell infiltration and elevating effector cytokines IFN-γ and TNF-α. By seamlessly coupling precise gene delivery with potent immune activation, this nanoplatform offers a compelling therapeutic strategy for colorectal cancer therapy.

title: Mild hydrostatic pressure preconditioning improves post-thaw motility of cryopreserved stallion semen.
abstract: The success of stallion semen cryopreservation is limited by substantial variation among stallions and by temporal variation within individual donors. However, the equine breeding industry requires predictable, stable, and efficient cryopreservation protocols to support the increasing use and dissemination of valuable genetics. One possible strategy for improving semen freezing is to introduce a preconditioning step before cryopreservation to prepare spermatozoa for the unavoidable stresses associated with freezing and thawing. This study evaluated the effects of mild hydrostatic pressure preconditioning on semen samples from Arabian and Shagya-Arabian stallions. Sixty-three semen samples from ten stallions were included in the study, spanning between July and April, in 31 collection days. Before routine cryopreservation, each sample was split into one control and six treatment aliquots, subjected to one of six hydrostatic pressure preconditioning treatments or maintained as control. After freezing and thawing, total motility (TM) and progressive motility (PM) were assessed using computer-assisted sperm analyser. Five of the six preconditioning treatments significantly improved both TM and PM compared with the control (p < 0.05). TM increased from 51.87% in control samples to 56.39-59.17% in mild-hydrostatic-pressure-treated samples, while PM increased from 39.56% to 43.81-47.00%. In our study, mild hydrostatic pressure preconditioning was readily integrated into the routine semen cryopreservation workflow and improved post-thaw motility. These findings indicate improved motility-based cryosurvival of stallion spermatozoa; however, the study did not assess pregnancy rate, foaling rate, or other in vivo fertility outcomes. Artificial insemination trials are therefore required before conclusions can be drawn regarding reproductive performance.

title: Leakage-aware pre-event machine learning evaluation for horse-race prediction under temporal validation.
abstract: Horse-racing prediction was used as a case study to develop and evaluate a leakage-aware machine-learning framework based on information available after race-entry finalization and before outcomes were known. Japanese Racing Association flat-race data obtained through JRA-VAN Data Lab. and exported using TARGET frontier JV were split temporally: 2015-2022 for training, 2023-2024 for validation, and January 5, 2025 to May 10, 2026 for independent testing. The test set contained 63,910 horse-level observations from 4,556 races. Confidence intervals were estimated using 10,000 race-level bootstrap resamples. Two horse-level binary outcome labels were evaluated: a win outcome and a JRA place-rule-compatible place outcome derived from the processed field_size variable. Compared with the augmented current_full_model, the hyperparameter-matched no-theory sensitivity-analysis model matched_no_theory_model performed better for both outcomes. For the win outcome, ROC AUC was 0.7543 (95% CI: 0.7475-0.7609) for matched_no_theory_model and 0.7293 (95% CI: 0.7224-0.7362) for current_full_model. For the JRA place-rule-compatible place outcome, ROC AUC was 0.7513 (95% CI: 0.7469-0.7558) and 0.7164 (95% CI: 0.7118-0.7212), respectively. An exploratory race-level uncertainty diagnostic was evaluated separately and was not incorporated into the horse-level prediction models. These findings indicate that the evaluated theory-score block did not improve temporal test-set performance. Domain-derived feature blocks should be evaluated incrementally through leakage audits, temporal validation, feature-block ablation, and matched sensitivity analyses before deployment.
